item.title: City of Ligonier Participates in Community Funding Resource Program
item.description: Treasurer Daniel Elliott announced that the Indiana Bond Bank assisted the city of Ligonier with project financing through its Community Funding Resource Program.

item.title: Under New Indiana Law, Changes To Vehicle’s Color Require Registration
item.description: The Indiana Bureau of Motor Vehicles is reminding Hoosiers of an update to Indiana Code that went into effect Thursday, Jan. 1.

item.title: Two years later, a $18,926 surgery claim is still in limbo, is there a way out?
item.description: Hien Shields faces an $18,926 bill for emergency spinal surgery after Anthem Blue Cross and its partner Carelon point fingers over authorization.

item.title: The wonderful words of Jesus
item.description: Why were the disciples’ hearts troubled?

item.title: Governor Restarting Workforce Board Months After Similar Board Was Eliminated
item.description: Indiana Gov. Mike Braun has re-established a board overseeing the state’s workforce training programs just months after a similar board was dissolved.

item.title: South Bend Offering Free Live Christmas Tree Recycling Program
item.description: South Bend residents can recycle their natural Christmas trees for free beginning Monday, Jan. 5, through a city-run collection program designed to turn holiday trees into mulch and compost.

item.title: St. Joseph County Farm Operates Indiana’s First Cheese Cave
item.description: Beneath the farmland of St. Joseph County, a family-run creamery is aging cheese in what is Indiana’s first underground cheese cave, using the natural conditions of the earth to shape flavor, texture and quality.

item.title: Kosciusko County Most Wanted
item.description: The Kosciusko County Sheriff’s Office is requesting assistance in finding people wanted on felony or misdemeanor warrants.

item.title: Winning Perennials for Your Gardens
item.description: When creating a new garden or looking for new additions, check out the Perennial Plants of the Year.

item.title: North Webster Community Public Library – Adult Winter Reading Program Begins
item.description: The North Webster Community Public Library invites patrons ages 18 and older to take part in its adult winter reading program, running now through Jan. 31.
